accountant.intro: Learn accounting from bookkeeping to financial statements to tax. This is the language of business — the skill every organisation, from market stall to government, needs to survive.

skillDomains.name: Financial Accounting
skillDomains.description: Record, summarise, and report financial transactions accurately.

skills.name: Bookkeeping
skills.description: The daily recording of business transactions.

modules.title: The double-entry system
modules.content:
Every transaction affects two accounts. This is the foundation of all accounting.

Debit and credit

  • Debit — left side of the account
  • Credit — right side of the account

The five types of accounts

  • Assets (things you own) — increase with debit
  • Liabilities (things you owe) — increase with credit
  • Equity (owner's stake) — increase with credit
  • Revenue (income) — increase with credit
  • Expenses (costs) — increase with debit

Every transaction: total debits = total credits. Always.

modules.title: Journals and ledgers
modules.content:
The journal

The first place transactions are recorded. Date, accounts affected, amounts, description.

The ledger

Grouped by account — all Cash transactions together, all Sales together, all Rent together.

Trial balance

A summary list of all ledger balances. Total debits must equal total credits. If not, there's an error.

The flow

Transaction → Journal → Ledger → Trial balance → Financial statements.

steps.q: You receive 500,000 Le in cash for services rendered. Journal entry?
steps.f: Cash (asset) increases — debit. Revenue increases — credit.

steps.q: You pay 100,000 Le rent for the month. Journal entry?
steps.f: Expense increases — debit. Cash decreases — credit.

steps.q: You buy equipment for 200,000 Le on credit (to pay next month). Journal entry?
steps.f: Asset (equipment) increases — debit. Liability (payable) increases — credit.

modules.title: Record a month of transactions
modules.prompt: Given a small business's transactions for one month (fictional but realistic), record them in a journal, post to ledgers, and produce a trial balance.
steps: Open a journal and record every transaction
Post each entry to the correct ledgers
Write a one-paragraph reflection on what was hardest

skills.name: Financial Statements
skills.description: The three reports every business lives by.

modules.title: The three core statements
modules.content:
1. Income Statement (Profit & Loss)

Revenue − Expenses = Profit. Shows performance over a period.

2. Balance Sheet

Assets = Liabilities + Equity. Shows position at a point in time.

3. Cash Flow Statement

Cash in − Cash out = Change in cash. Shows liquidity over a period.

All three connect. Net income from the income statement flows to equity on the balance sheet and appears on the cash flow statement.

modules.title: Read a real income statement
modules.prompt: A small business has the following for the year: Revenue 12,000,000 Le; Cost of goods sold 7,200,000 Le; Rent 800,000 Le; Salaries 2,000,000 Le; Utilities 400,000 Le; Marketing 300,000 Le. Calculate gross profit, operating profit, and net profit. What does each number tell you?
modules.context: Being able to read a statement quickly is a core professional skill.

skills.name: Costing
skills.description: Know what your product actually costs.

modules.title: Direct vs indirect costs
modules.content:
Direct costs

Can be traced to a specific product. Materials, direct labour.

Indirect costs (overhead)

Support the whole business. Rent, management salaries, utilities.

Why it matters

To price a product, you need its full cost — direct PLUS a share of overhead. Many small businesses forget the overhead and price too low.

How to allocate overhead

Simple method: divide total overhead by total units produced. Crude but works for small businesses.

steps.q: Direct materials: 5,000 Le. Direct labour: 2,000 Le. Total monthly overhead 3,000,000 Le ÷ 1,000 units = 3,000 Le per unit. Full cost?
A competitor sells a similar product for 8,000 Le. Your full cost is 10,000 Le. What do you do?
o: Match their price and lose 2,000 per sale
Investigate — reduce your cost or differentiate
steps.f: If your cost is above their price, you must either cut costs or justify a premium. Do not sell at a loss.

steps.q: You produce 1,500 units instead of 1,000, with same overhead. What happens to overhead per unit?
steps.f: 3,000,000 ÷ 1,500 = 2,000 Le per unit. Higher volume spreads fixed costs.

skills.name: Budgeting
skills.description: Plan the money before it moves.

modules.title: Why budgets matter
modules.content:
A budget is a plan for money. Without one, spending follows opportunity, and the business drifts.

Types of budgets

  • Operating budget — revenue and expenses for the year
  • Cash budget — timing of cash in and out
  • Capital budget — major purchases (equipment, vehicles)

How to build one

  1. Start with realistic revenue (based on history, not hope)
  2. List all expenses (variable and fixed)
  3. Calculate expected profit
  4. Compare to last year to see trends
  5. Review monthly against actuals

modules.title: Build a simple business budget
modules.prompt: For a small business of your choice (real or fictional), build a one-year operating budget with monthly breakdowns. Include revenue, variable costs, fixed costs, and profit.
steps: List variable costs per unit or month

skillDomains.name: Audit & Tax
skillDomains.description: Compliance and verification — the legal backbone of accounting.

skills.name: Taxation
skills.description: Understand tax obligations for individuals and businesses.

modules.title: The tax categories
modules.content:
Businesses and individuals in West Africa typically deal with:

  • Income tax — on profit
  • VAT (Value Added Tax) — on sales (15% in many ECOWAS countries, 7.5% in Nigeria, 15% in Ghana, 15% in Sierra Leone)
  • Payroll tax / PAYE — deducted from employee salaries
  • Withholding tax — deducted from payments to suppliers
  • Corporate tax — on company profit (rate varies by country)

The accountant's role

Calculate correctly, file on time, keep records. Late filing penalties can destroy small businesses.

steps.q: A business sells goods for 1,150,000 Le including 15% VAT. How much is the VAT?
An employee earns 500,000 Le gross per month. PAYE is calculated on this. Why does the employer deduct it?
o: Because the employer is legally responsible for collecting and remitting employee tax
steps.f: Employers are tax collection agents. Failure to remit PAYE is a serious offence.

steps.q: When is VAT typically due in most West African countries?
o: Monthly, by the 15th or 21st of the following month
steps.f: VAT is usually filed monthly with a specific deadline. Missing it triggers penalties.

skillDomains.name: Software
skillDomains.description: The tools modern accountants use daily.

modules.title: What software can do
modules.content:
Manual bookkeeping on paper is slow and error-prone. Accounting software:

  • Records transactions quickly
  • Prevents arithmetic errors
  • Generates statements automatically
  • Tracks tax liability in real time
  • Produces reports on demand

Common options in West Africa

  • Spreadsheets (Excel, Google Sheets) — free, flexible, manual
  • QuickBooks — industry standard, paid
  • Sage — common with larger businesses
  • Zoho Books — cloud-based, cheaper
  • Local options — various country-specific tools

Whatever the tool, the accounting principles are the same.

steps.q: A market stall owner needs simple bookkeeping. Best tool?
o: Pen and notebook, or a simple Google Sheet
steps.f: Match tool to complexity. Simple business, simple tool.

steps.q: A 50-employee business needs payroll, tax filing, and monthly financials. Best tool?
steps.f: At this scale, real software pays for itself in time saved and errors avoided.

steps.q: What's the main advantage of cloud-based accounting software?
o: Access from anywhere; automatic backup; collaboration
steps.f: Cloud means access and backup. Useful for accountants with multiple clients.

skillDomains.name: Ethics
skillDomains.description: The professional standards that make accounting trustworthy.

skills.name: Professional Ethics
skills.description: Integrity is the accountant's only asset.

modules.title: The five principles
modules.content:
Every accounting professional body requires these:

  1. Integrity — be straightforward and honest
  2. Objectivity — don't let bias, conflict of interest, or undue influence override professional judgement
  3. Professional competence — maintain the skills and knowledge required
  4. Confidentiality — do not disclose client information without authority
  5. Professional behaviour — comply with laws and avoid discrediting the profession

A single ethical failure ends a career. There is no recovery from fraud.

modules.title: Face an ethical pressure
modules.prompt: Your client (a business owner) asks you to record a personal expense as a business expense, so they can deduct it for tax. They say 'everyone does it'. How do you respond?
modules.context: Ethical pressure is constant in accounting. How you respond defines your career.
